name: FinDelta
intro: Financial numerical reasoning with audited labels and evidence-bound arithmetic.
question: How do training duration, arithmetic execution, and label quality affect numerical reasoning over financial reports?
work: Built a FinQA data pipeline, LoRA SFT and DPO experiments, an arithmetic executor that checks operands against evidence, and matched label-repair comparisons across three seeds.
data: Custom company-separated FinQA cohort; 1,000 original training questions and 200 development questions. The reviewed training cohort retains 966 questions. Experiments use Qwen3-0.6B.
finding: Longer SFT improved development accuracy with the same executor. Small-scale DPO did not confirm a gain, and the three-seed label-repair difference remained small.
limit: Results use a custom development cohort, not official FinQA leaderboard scores. The final test set has not been evaluated, and executor gains must be distinguished from training gains.

name: TAQ Event Lab
intro: Controlled comparisons of trade-event tokenization under exposure and compute budgets.
question: How do joint event tokens and sequential field tokens behave when the comparison budget changes?
work: Implemented small Transformer baselines, cleaning audits, train-only quantization, repeated-seed comparisons, downstream direction tasks, and frozen-representation probes.
data: TAQ trades for AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, and NVDA over ten trading days in February 2025. NVDA supplies the unseen-stock comparison; raw and prepared market records are excluded from the repository.
finding: Experiments show that model rankings depend on the exposure or training-time budget. Repeated seeds and downstream probes extend the likelihood comparison.
limit: The sample has few dates, and some test results were inspected during development. Token likelihood and representation probes do not establish trading profitability.

name: IV Surface Lab
intro: Surface construction, time audits, and rolling return and variance forecasts.
question: Do implied-volatility features add information beyond price-history and HAR benchmarks?
work: Built a shared surface, price, and calendar pipeline; interpolation and node-quality checks; dividend-aware labels; rolling forecasts; and exploratory residualized-skew extensions.
data: optionsDX SPX daily option chains for 2010–2023 and CRSP SPY data. Vendor raw records and processed market inputs are excluded; a separate synthetic demo is available.
finding: The initial specified one-day return comparison improved holdout MSE by 0.087% with p=0.590. IV levels supplied variance-forecasting information in the recorded sample.
limit: Return evidence is weak. Stronger variance significance depends on the multiple-comparison family. Later extensions reuse the original sample and former holdout, so their findings are exploratory.

name: Ethereum Modularity
intro: Exploratory links between on-chain community structure and equity volatility events.
question: Is Ethereum transaction-network modularity associated with unusually large SPY returns?
work: Implemented hourly weighted graphs, Louvain modularity, UTC panel assembly, event studies, regressions with HAC standard errors, and alternative thresholds and graph weights.
data: Google BigQuery Ethereum transactions, with SPY observations through Yahoo Finance adapters. The configured main sample is 2024, with a separate COVID case study.
finding: The original project reports falling modularity around equity volatility events, opposite to its initial hypothesis. The archived lag-one ROC figure displays AUC=0.618.
limit: The current code evaluates ROC on the fitted sample. That AUC is an in-sample fit statistic. Source panels and numerical tables are absent, and network association does not identify a causal mechanism.

name: AAPL LSTM Prototype
intro: An early prototype connecting a return-sequence classifier with a broker adapter.
question: How can a classifier over recent open-price returns connect to a paper-trading workflow?
work: Implemented stacked LSTMs, chronological data splitting, model persistence, connection checks, and an Alpaca paper-trading adapter.
data: 1,589 AAPL 30-minute bars from January 23 through July 21, 2025, with OHLC, volume, trade count, and VWAP. Training inputs use ten open-price returns.
finding: The repository demonstrates the components of the workflow. Its existing backtest is a prototype diagnostic rather than validated strategy performance.
limit: Target/P&L timing, separately adapted label thresholds, and inconsistent backtest windows require correction. Costs and complete position accounting are not included.
